title: Driven Meteorological Modeling: Transforming Wind Speed and Direction Prediction
summary: Researchers are developing a wind-model proof of concept for the Red Sea coast and Gulf of Suez, with operational validation still planned.
source_collection: ITU AI for Good: Innovate for Impact (2025)
account: The project proposes AI forecasting of wind speed and direction for wind farms, grids, and extreme-weather planning. A prototype and historical benchmark comparisons are in development. The source does not quantify an achieved generation, dispatch, or safety benefit.
purpose: Improve wind forecasts for energy operations and severe-weather planning.
system: Driven Meteorological Modeling: Transforming Wind Speed and Direction Prediction
location: Red Sea coast, Saudi Arabia, and Gulf of Suez, Egypt (planned study regions)

ratings.reason: The Red Sea/Gulf of Suez wind model is a proof of concept under development, without an observed wind-farm operational gain.
Grid resilience and climate-risk reduction are potential uses.

ai_role.statement: The contributor describes the system and its proposed or reported contribution. This collection entry does not independently isolate the effect of AI from the surrounding workflow.

evidence.citation: Contributed use case in International Telecommunication Union, AI for Good: Innovate for Impact, 2025. Information current as of June 2025. The reported outcomes are attributed to the submitting project, not an independent outcome evaluation by ITU.
evidence.title: Use Case 21: Driven Meteorological Modeling: Transforming Wind Speed and Direction Prediction

produced_by: The contributor describes the application and its setting in the cited entry. Conditions sufficient to reproduce the reported benefit have not been established.
must_hold: Requirements for reproducing the benefit need to be evaluated in the new setting. The collection entry does not establish that its reported results will recur.

headline: Wind-forecast AI targets energy and climate decisions

revisions.change: Added the sourced case with separate benefit depth, beneficiary, evidence confidence, and outcome status assessments.

claim_basis: The makers' report is on file. There is no independent source and no finding by a regulator or court.
